Start from each `Order_Items` record; combine it with each `Customer_Orders` record for which Order ID (`Customer_Orders.Order_ID`) equals Order ID (`Order_Items.Order_ID`), one combined record per match (a record without a match is dropped); combine it with each `Stores` record for which Store ID (`Stores.Store_ID`) equals Store ID (`Customer_Orders.Store_ID`) (compared as numbers: the text is read as a number), one combined record per match (a record without a match is dropped); combine it with each `Marketing_Regions` record for which Marketing Region Code (`Marketing_Regions.Marketing_Region_Code`) equals Marketing Region Code (`Stores.Marketing_Region_Code`) (compared as text, character by character), one combined record per match (a record without a match is dropped); group the kept records by Order ID (`Order_Items.Order_ID`) and market priority description (`Marketing_Regions.Marketing_Region_Descriptrion`); each group gives one result row; for each result row, return (1) Order ID (`Order_Items.Order_ID`); (2) market priority description (`Marketing_Regions.Marketing_Region_Descriptrion`); (3) the average of quantity ordered (`Order_Items.Order_Quantity`) in the group (missing values ignored; missing when there are none).
Step 2. Start from the rows of step 1; all kept records form one group, which gives one result row; for each result row, return (1) the average of column (3) of step 1 in the group (missing values ignored; missing when there are none).
Step 3. Start from the rows of step 1; combine it with the rows of step 2 for which it is not true that column (1) of step 2 is missing, one combined record per match (a record without a match is dropped); for each kept record, return (1) column (1) of step 1; (2) column (2) of step 1; (3) column (3) of step 1; (4) A ÷ B. Here A is column (3) of step 1; B is column (1) of step 2.
Step 4. Start from the rows of step 3; group the kept records by column (2) of step 3; each group gives one result row; for each result row, return (1) column (2) of step 3; (2) the average of column (4) of step 3 in the group (missing values ignored; missing when there are none).
Step 5. Start from the rows of step 3; combine it with the rows of step 4 for which column (2) of step 3 equals column (1) of step 4 (compared as text, character by character), one combined record per match (a record without a match is dropped); keep only the records for which column (4) of step 3 is greater than column (2) of step 4; for each kept record, return (1) column (1) of step 3; (2) column (2) of step 3; (3) column (3) of step 3; (4) column (4) of step 3; (5) A − B. Here A is column (4) of step 3; B is column (2) of step 4.
Step 6. Start from the rows of step 5; group the kept records by column (2) of step 5; each group gives one result row; for each result row, return (1) column (2) of step 5; (2) the average of column (3) of step 5 in the group (missing values ignored; missing when there are none); (3) the average of column (4) of step 5 in the group (missing values ignored; missing when there are none); (4) the average of column (5) of step 5 in the group (missing values ignored; missing when there are none).
Step 7 (the answer). Start from the rows of step 6; all kept records form one group, which gives one result row; for each result row, return (1) the average of column (2) of step 6 in the group (missing values ignored; missing when there are none); (2) the average of column (3) of step 6 in the group (missing values ignored; missing when there are none); (3) the average of column (4) of step 6 in the group (missing values ignored; missing when there are none).
